correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundaries k=1 versus k≥2 are explicit. The greedy-arch lemma has a constructive missing subsequence proof; at 2k the only potential Lyndon candidate is a proper power; at 2k+1 the no-00 case yields exactly one doubled-one gap and the 00 case forces 001 followed by k−1 permutation arches and rules out every 10 block by a strictly smaller rotation. Two witnesses meet universality and the Lyndon condition. Independent brute-force checks used literal rotations for all binary words at lengths 2k,2k+1 for k≤8 and direct subsequences for k≤5. These finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question is a natural extremal intersection of two classical string classes: scattered-subsequence universality and Lyndon necklace representatives. It gives a sharp one-symbol cost together with an all-index classification and exactly two extremizers, distinguishing the binary case from ternary, where 012021 is already a length-six 2-universal Lyndon word. It is not a fixed-size table or a parameter-renamed general bound; the nontrivial lexicographic rotation exclusion supplies a reusable structural mechanism.
